title: Nagasaki's harbor Rising
premise: In the frozen port city of Nagasaki's harbor district, Cyrus Whitlock works by lamplight in her father's print shop, cutting typefaces and keeping her head down as revolutionary pamphlets circulate through the winter streets. When a half-drowned stranger, Tomas Reyes, stumbles in carrying letters in the unmistakable hand of Aldous Vane—a magistrate officially executed two years ago—Cyrus realizes the regime's founding atrocity was a lie, and the proof sits in her own type drawer: the forged execution warrant she once set without knowing. Hunted by the magistrate's true killers, Cyrus and Tomas must carry the evidence past three harbor checkpoints and onto the last ship before the river ice breaks and the harbor seals for the season. At the third checkpoint, Cyrus trades her father's safety—and her own anonymity—for the truth, choosing to print the confession in ten thousand copies as the ice groans and splits, igniting the revolution she spent her life avoiding.
about_author: Beatrix Vane is the pen name of a former typesetter who spent a decade restoring letterpress equipment in northern port towns. She writes historical fiction about the invisible hands behind the printed word.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Cyrus Whitlock, POV. In the print shop above the frozen harbor, Cyrus sorts type by feel in the dark, measuring her life in what can be carried and what must be left. Emotional beat: quiet, watchful endurance—the discipline of invisibility established.

chapters.title: Pamphlets in the Snow
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Revolutionary broadsides flood the market; her father quietly refuses a commission to print counter-edicts, endangering them both. Cyrus burns the drafts. Emotional beat: first crack in the family's neutrality, fear sharpening into unease.

chapters.title: The Man from the Ice
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. A half-frozen stranger, Tomas Reyes, collapses against the shop door at closing, clutching an oilskin packet. She drags him inside against her better judgment. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion overriding survival instinct.

chapters.title: A Dead Man's Hand
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. He reveals letters in the handwriting of Aldous Vane, the magistrate executed two years ago—proof the execution was staged and the warrant forged. Emotional beat: desperate hope colliding with the terror of what the evidence demands.

chapters.title: What the Type Remembers
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus recognizes the forged warrant's typeface—her own cutting, set by her own hand two years past. She has been an unwitting instrument of the lie. Emotional beat: guilt and vertigo; invisibility revealed as complicity.

chapters.title: Her Father's Silence
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. She confronts her father, who admits he knew the warrant was false and printed it to keep the shop alive. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into understanding—the price of survival made personal.

chapters.title: Boots on the Stair
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. Regime inspectors search the quarter for a fugitive; the shop is ransacked while Cyrus hides the packet inside a font case of broken type. Emotional beat: claustrophobic terror, the first hunt begun.

chapters.title: The Harbormaster's Price
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. Tomas seeks passage from a corrupt harbormaster who names an impossible price: the letters themselves. Emotional beat: the dawning knowledge that every ally is also a seller.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. They map the route: the fish market gate, the customs bridge, the ice-breaker quay. Each checkpoint demands papers they cannot forge—except by a forger's daughter. Emotional beat: grim resolve replacing panic.

chapters.title: Lessons in Forgery
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus teaches Tomas to cut a passable seal and forge a customs chit; he teaches her the streets of the smugglers' quarter. Emotional beat: wary partnership deepening into trust, almost tenderness.

chapters.title: The Fish Market Gate
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. First checkpoint: they pass the gate hidden among herring barrels, but a guard recognizes Tomas's face from a wanted bill. Emotional beat: breath-held tension, escape by seconds.

chapters.title: An Old Debt
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus seeks out Maren, her father's estranged former apprentice, now a smuggler, who agrees to help—for a favor Cyrus cannot yet name. Emotional beat: the cost of calling in old loyalties.

chapters.title: What Maren Wants
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. Maren's price revealed: the print shop itself, once the ice breaks, as her route inland. Cyrus must choose between her inheritance and the mission. Emotional beat: bargaining with the future, grief disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: The Customs Bridge
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. Second checkpoint: the forged chit nearly fails; a sympathetic clerk—a secret sympathizer—waves them through but warns them the quay is watched. Emotional beat: fragile hope, the discovery that resistance has quiet allies.

chapters.title: The Warrant's Other Signer
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus deciphers a second signature on the forged warrant: Colonel Ashe, now the harbor's commandant—keeper of the third checkpoint. Emotional beat: the trap closing; the enemy is the gate itself.

chapters.title: Her Father Taken
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. The regime arrests her father as leverage, leaving a message: the letters for the printer. Emotional beat: devastation and the terrible clarity of what loyalty now demands.

chapters.title: Loyalty or Truth
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. Tomas urges they flee with the evidence and let her father hang; Cyrus refuses. Their partnership fractures. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh—loyalty versus truth, and the impossibility of choosing cleanly.

chapters.title: The Print Shop at Midnight
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Instead of surrendering the letters, Cyrus sets the confession in type—ten thousand copies of the truth—and Maren's smugglers distribute them through the quarter overnight. Emotional beat: transformation; the invisible woman becomes the voice.

chapters.title: The Quay at Dawn
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. Third checkpoint: Ashe waits at the ice-breaker quay as the river ice groans and splits. Cyrus walks out openly, offering the original letters in exchange for her father. Emotional beat: the climax's terrible stillness before the break.

chapters.title: When the Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. The pamphlets flood the checkpoint; dockworkers and soldiers, having read them overnight, refuse Ashe's orders. In the chaos, Cyrus's father is freed and Ashe falls to his own men. Emotional beat: cathartic eruption—the revolution arriving not with armies but with ink.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. The ship departs with the evidence bound for the capital; Cyrus stays behind, choosing the city that needs printers more than witnesses. Tomas sails alone. Emotional beat: bittersweet parting; survival redefined as staying.

chapters.title: The First Honest Page
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Weeks later, the shop—shared now with Maren—prints the harbor's first free newspaper, her father setting type beside her. Cyrus measures the world no longer in what can be carried, but in what can be told. Emotional beat: hard-won peace; justice outside the law, made ordinary.
